$comment: THE DEPLOY TARGET, DECLARED. Fifteen gates run before a change lands here and past the
merge there was nothing: no environment manifest, no drift check, nothing an agent could
read to know what runs where. Vercel's project settings are a dashboard, and a dashboard is
not reviewable, not diffable and not reversible — so 'the production environment drifted
from what the repo assumes' was a state no check in this repository could go red for.
This file is the smallest declaration of that target which is still worth diffing in a pull
request: the runtime the platform must give us, the schedules it must fire, and every
environment variable the deployment reads, each one classified by what happens when it is
absent. `npm run env:manifest` prints it; `npm run env:manifest:check` diffs it against the
repository's own sources and fails on drift, and the same comparison runs on every build in
test-unit/environment-manifest.test.mjs (blocking, inside `npm run test:unit` → `check:ci`
→ .husky/pre-push).
BE EXACT ABOUT WHAT THIS CAN AND CANNOT SEE. Everything below is checked against COMMITTED
data — package.json, vercel.json, next.config.ts, .env.example, docs/deploy.md, the
workflows. So it catches the drift that starts in the repository: a cron added to vercel.json
and to no schedule anyone declared, a Node bump in one workflow and not the others, a new
env var read by the code and classified nowhere, a variable that must never be set in
production quietly moving into the required list. It CANNOT read the Vercel project: what
is actually configured there today, whether a secret is set, which region a function runs
in. That half needs an API token and is the operator's (docs/deploy.md § Post-deploy
verification) — `cannotSee` below says so in the file rather than leaving a reader to
assume otherwise.
WHEN THIS GOES RED, the fix is never to delete the row: the row firing IS the drift being
caught. Move the declaration in the same diff as the change it describes, which is one line
a reviewer reads next to the other.

runtime.$comment: What the platform must give us. Each value is compared against the file named in `from`.

ciNode.why: the format goldens pin byte-identical Intl output, and ICU moves across Node minors — docs/deploy.md § Node version authority

nextConfig.why: dynamic-by-default with no implicit caching; a route segment-config opt-out would un-cache a whole route, which is why lint block adamant/route-segment-config refuses one

timezone.why: the date goldens are minted in the product's home market

environments.promotion: push. Vercel ships master on push, so the push IS the release act — there is no PR stage between a developer and production (docs/deploy.md § Delivery contract).
environments.gate: .husky/pre-push runs `npm run check:ci` before any push that updates master; the same checks are required status checks on a pull request (.github/required-checks.json, .github/branch-ruleset.json).
environments.rollback: docs/deploy.md § Deploy + rollback (Vercel) — re-alias the previous deployment; the operator's action, rehearsed weekly by .github/workflows/revert-drill.yml for everything that needs no production access.

environments.promotion: automatic per push to a non-default branch; never aliased to the production domain.
environments.gate: the same required checks run on the pull request.
environments.rollback: not applicable — a preview is discarded, never promoted.

environments.promotion: none — `npm run dev:local` (DEV_AUTH=true LOCAL_DB=true) is the fully offline authenticated product.

crons.$comment: Declared here and compared set-for-set against vercel.json, and each path must resolve to a route module. Every one is guarded by CRON_SECRET through src/lib/cron-auth.ts, which fails CLOSED when the secret is unset.

schedules.does: weekly digest to the operator's destination

productionForbidden.$comment: Variables that must never be set in the production environment. The code fuses DEV_AUTH and LOCAL_DB when NODE_ENV=production, but an unset variable is the only configuration that cannot rot (docs/deploy.md § Pre-deploy checklist). A name here may not also be classified `required` or `optional`.

cannotSee: what is actually configured in the Vercel project today — this reads the repository, not the platform
whether a declared secret is SET, and what its value is (that is `npm run doctor` locally and the operator's dashboard in production)
function region, memory and concurrency, which Vercel decides from its own defaults and the per-route `maxDuration` exports
the Firestore TTL policy on `llmTelemetry`, which is created once per project with gcloud and is not code-deployable (docs/deploy.md § Telemetry retention)
DNS, the custom domain and the production alias — all of them operator actions under their own account
$env: Every variable the deployment reads, classified by what its absence costs. `class`:
required   production does not work correctly without it.
optional   a feature degrades — usually to demo or to log-only — and the app still works.
local      a local-development switch; several are also on `productionForbidden` above.
bench      read by a benchmark or a drill, never by the serving app.
build      read at build time only, never at runtime; not in .env.example by design.
`scope`: `server` (never reaches the browser) or `public` (NEXT_PUBLIC_, published by
construction — a secret here is a published secret, which is what SAST rule
`public-env-secret` refuses). `source: env-example` means the name must appear in
.env.example, which is the annotated reference a human reads.

SKLIK_WRITES_ENABLED.note: AGENTS.md § Red. Only the exact value "1" arms real Sklik mutations; it stays unset until the owner's live proof (docs/deploy.md § Sklik writes). Never set, widen or model a second guard on this.

RESEND_API_KEY.note: a two-in-one switch: it also arms real twin delivery to a customer's customers (docs/deploy.md § Environment variables).

NEXT_PUBLIC_SOURCE_REPO_URL.note: proposed, not yet read by the app — docs/open-source/self-hosting.md.

LOCAL_DB.note: fused off in production EXCEPT under SELF_HOSTED=true, where the sqlite store IS the data layer — which is why it is not on productionForbidden.

ADAMANT_DOCKER_BUILD.note: next.config.ts — emits the standalone server for container builds only. Never set on Vercel.

DEV_INSPECT.note: next.config.ts — registers the dev-inspector Turbopack loader; set only by `npm run dev:inspect`.
